paper_metadata.title: Tensile Creep Properties of Cr-Si Alloys at 980 °C in Air—Influence of Ge and Mo Addition

evidence.quote: The tensile creep behavior of Cr-Si alloys with Cr ≥ 91 at.% was investigated in air at 980 ◦C with a constant load of 50–100 MPa.

The investigated alloys in this work are a binary alloy consisting of Cr and 9 at.% Si (Cr91Si9) and two ternary alloys consisting of 7 at.% Si and 2 at.% Ge or Mo, respectively (Cr91Si7Ge2 and Cr91Si7Mo2).

The samples still reach elongation in the range of up to 23% for loads ≥ 75MPa and additionally show a decrease in creep rate by one order of magnitude.

Nitrogen and oxygen usually pass the Cr2O3 scale by a stepwise scale cracking and microcrack formation mechanism.
At high temperatures, not only impurities but also oxygen and nitrogen affect the properties through internal oxidation and nitridation.
It was also observed under isothermal oxidation [9] that nitridation proceeds into the substrate even without load along the grain boundaries, especially for binary Cr-Si alloys.
After longer exposures in air at high temperatures and lower loads (50 MPa), internal nitridation is observed to influence the creep strength of these alloys.
